title: R_5(3(x-y)=2z) > 350: first five-colour bound for this family
statement: The 5-colour Rado number of 3(x-y) = 2z exceeds 350. No five-colour Rado number of the family a(x-y)=bz appears in the literature, whose tables stop at four colours. The bound also establishes that this work's shell construction, which gives 319 at (a,k)=(3,5), is NOT TIGHT at k=5 -- in contrast to k=3 and k=4, where it is attained at every point tested.

concept_refs.note: authored this session at math-education graph/concepts/rado-number.md (uncommitted)

provenance.conjectured_by: construction: the general-k lower bound derived in this work predicted 319 as a candidate exact value at (a,k)=(3,5); the prediction was tested and the tightness half failed
searched_by: axeyum cube-and-conquer (agent_cube, branch 2,3,4,6, k=5): reported the instance SATISFIABLE after 14.8 s, refuting the tightness expectation
axeyum native proof-producing CDCL: independently re-derived a satisfying model in 32.3 s
checked_by: scripts/check-claim-certificates.py witness replay (independent O(n^2) enumerator, 22,472 solution triples enumerated)

prior_art.citation: Y. Chang, J. A. De Loera, W. J. Wesley, 'Rado Numbers and SAT Computations', ISSAC 2022
prior_art.establishes: R_3 and partial R_4 tables for this family. No k=5 values; their Lemma 4.2 (the b=a-1 construction) is stated for k=3 only.

prior_art.citation: A. C. Li, 'On Rado Numbers for x+by=bz: The b^k Pattern and a Threshold Conjecture', SSRN 6814341 (2026)
prior_art.establishes: Reports R_5(3) > 296 > 243 in the b=1 column, i.e. non-tightness of the a^k law at k=5. Not peer-reviewed; full text not read (paywalled). Our independent finding is the b=a-1 analogue.

evidence.notes: A 5-colouring of [350] using all five colours, no monochromatic solution among the 27,028 solution triples. Reached by incremental climbing from the verified 319 witness, one integer at a time with warm restarts; the climb stalled at 351, so 350 is the search's limit rather than a proven threshold.

evidence.supports: R_5 > 319 (lower bound, strictly exceeding the construction's bound of 319)
evidence.notes: A 5-colouring of [319] using all five colours, with no monochromatic solution among the 22,472 solution triples in [319]^2. Verified by axeyum's own model self-check and by an independent brute-force enumerator sharing no code with the generator.

known: R_5(3(x-y)=2z) > 350, witnessed and verified (evidence row witness-350); the earlier 319 witness is retained as the point that refuted tightness

The shell construction of this work yields a verified solution-free colouring of [N] with N+1 = a^k + a^(k-1) - 2a + 1; this is ATTAINED at (a,k)=(3,3) [31], (4,3) [73], (3,4) [103] and (4,4) [313], all independently re-verified, but NOT at (3,5), where it gives 318 while a 5-colouring of [319] exists. The general-k proof is asserted in the construction source and has NOT been independently verified here.
Independent corroboration of k=5 non-tightness in a different column: Li (SSRN 6814341) reports R_5(3)>296>243 for b=1
The incremental climb stalled at 351 after warm-restart retries; that is a search limit, not evidence of a threshold
frontier.would_settle: A verified 5-colouring of [n-1] together with an exhaustive cube cover refuting [n], for the same n. Both artifact kinds and their checkers exist in this family; the obstruction is the cost of refutation at k=5, not the encoding.
frontier.attack_notes: The satisfiable side is cheap here (14.8 s by cube search, 32.3 s by monolithic CDCL), so the lower bound can be pushed far. The refutation side at five colours is untested at any n and is the real question.

notes: Recorded because a failed prediction is evidence. The construction's bound remains SOUND -- a lower bound cannot be refuted by finding a larger colouring -- but its tightness, which holds at k=3 and k=4, does not extend to k=5. This is the datum that scopes every tightness claim in this work to k <= 4.
